guardian.title: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo now deadliest in country’s history
guardian.description:
At least 2,325 people have died from the virus, according to official data, with outbreak on track to be biggest in history

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is now the deadliest in the country’s history, with at least 2,325 people dead, according to government data, surpassing the toll from the 2018-20 outbreak.

The DRC’s public health institute said confirmed cases had risen to 4,945, including 101 detected in the previous 24 hours.

guardian.description:

Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe, taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday.

euronews.description: The facility will research and test technology designed to detect and counter unauthorised drones around airports, major events and critical infrastructure.

rfi.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot on Tuesday became the first French woman to perform a spacewalk, carrying out a mission to repair a communications system on the International Space Station (ISS).

rfi.title: Warnings sent to French taxpayers after hackers allegedly sell stolen data
rfi.description: More than 670,000 French taxpayers are being notified that their personal and tax information has been stolen in cyber attacks on the French tax office and allegedly sold online.

rfi.title: DRC authorities warn Ebola outbreak is worst to date and yet to peak
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s latest Ebola outbreak has become the deadliest in the country’s history, surpassing the devastating 2018-2020 epidemic even as health authorities warn that the current outbreak is yet to reach its peak.

rfi.title: Liechtenstein changes royal succession rules, giving women equal rights
rfi.description: Liechtenstein has announced a change in its order of succession, doing away with male heir priority and giving women equal rights to the throne.

rfi.description: Zambia's electoral commission has announced that Hakainde Hichilema has been re-elected president after a race that critics said was tightly managed by his government.

rfi.title: French PM Lecornu says aid available 'immediately' to rebuild fire-hit regions
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Monday announced aid worth €12 million to help residents of the southwest hit by wildfires rebuild their lives. He was heckled earlier in the day by dozens of locals in the town of Le Porge in the Gironde region, who said they were unhappy with the government's response.

rfi.title: Iran bars two French diplomats over alleged 'interference'
rfi.description: Iran has said ​that two French embassy employees who were briefly detained last month following a ​diplomatic dispute will not be allowed to return to Iran.

rfi.title: Cop17 aims to restore land and hope in fight against desertification
rfi.description: Extreme weather across much of Europe and elsewhere is lending added weight to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (Cop17), which begins on Monday in Mongolia. RFI looks at what's at stake worldwide.

rfi.title: Devastated by wildfire, the village of Le Porge pins hopes for support on PM visit
rfi.description: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will visit the Gironde department in southwestern France on Monday to launch reconstruction efforts, after the area fell victim to the most destructive wildfires seen in 70 years. The mayor of Le Porge – one of the villages worst affected – told RFI he's hoping for government support to rebuild its economy, which relies heavily on forest exploitation.

rfi.title: Cameroon beat Malawi to claim maiden Women’s Cup of Nations title
rfi.description: Cameroon claimed a first Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title when they beat Malawi 3-0 in Sunday's final in Morocco, with Marie Ngah Manga’s first-half double helping the the Indomitable Lionesses seal victory.

rfi.title: Ex-PM Attal urges Macron to put under-15 social media ban to referendum
rfi.description: Gabriel Attal has called on President Emmanuel Macron to put a proposed ban on social media for children under 15 directly to French voters, after the Constitutional Council struck down legislation approved by parliament.

rfi.title: Belgium turns to European air support as wildfire rages near German border
rfi.description: Belgium called in aerial reinforcements from across Europe on Sunday as firefighters battled the country’s largest wildfire in more than a century, with flames spreading rapidly through a difficult-to-reach nature reserve near the German border.

rfi.title: Obesity rises sharply as French Polynesia faces chronic health challenges
rfi.description: French Polynesia is facing growing public health pressures as rising rates of chronic disease combine with an ageing population and changing lifestyles. More than half of adult residents are now considered obese.

rfi.title: Armenian Genocide survivors' grandson says 'political motives' block recognition
rfi.description: In 1915, the Ottoman Empire began the systematic deportation and massacre of its Armenian population. As many as 1.5 million Armenians were killed – widely regarded by historians as the twentieth century's first genocide, and the event for which the term was later coined. Stephan Pechdimaldji, the grandson of two of the survivors, spoke to RFI about why recognition still matters.

rfi.title: Law on assisted dying wins constitutional approval in France
rfi.description: France's Constitutional Council on Friday approved a law creating a right to assisted dying, removing the last major legal obstacle before the measure can be enacted and implemented.

zeit.title: Türkei: Erdoğan unterzeichnet Amnestiegesetz für PKK-Mitglieder
zeit.description: Ein neues Gesetz in der Türkei sieht Straferleichterungen für PKK-Mitglieder vor. Umgesetzt werden soll es aber erst nach Auflösung der verbotenen Organisation.

zeit.title: Thüringen: Mario Voigt sieht Landesregierung nicht durch BSW-Abweichler bedroht
zeit.description: Zwei BSW-Abgeordnete in Thüringen wollen die Koalition mit CDU und SPD nicht mehr mittragen. Ministerpräsident Voigt betont den Rückhalt beim Großteil der BSW-Fraktion.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Burnham sichert Ukraine trotz russischer Drohungen Hilfe zu
zeit.description: Die britische Regierung will sich durch Warnungen Russlands nicht einschüchtern lassen. Zehn Menschen sterben bei russischen Raketenangriffen auf Charkiw. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Drohnenfund am Flughafen Leipzig: Dobrindt vermutet Zusammenhang von Leipzig mit anderen Anschlagsplänen
zeit.description: »Leipzig ist Teil eines größeren Gebildes«, sagt Bundesinnenminister Alexander Dobrindt. Das Anschlagsszenario sei kein Einzelfall, das Gesamtbild werde nun ermittelt.

zeit.title: AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt: Das Bauhaus wäre erst der Anfang
zeit.description: Vor der Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt hat die AfD ihren kulturpolitischen Hauptfeind gefunden: das Bauhaus. An ihrem Kampf dagegen zeigt sich eine radikale Version der Partei.

france24fr.title: Yvette Roudy, première "ministre des Droits de la femme", est morte
france24fr.description: La première "ministre des Droits de la femme" entre 1981 et 1986, Yvette Roudy, est décédée mardi à l'âge de 97 ans à Cabestany (Pyrénées-orientales). Socialiste, elle a fait voter le remboursement de l'IVG et laissé son nom à la loi de 1983 sur l'égalité professionnelle entre les femmes et les hommes.

france24fr.title: Sophie Adenot a débuté sa sortie dans l'espace, une première pour une astronaute française
france24fr.description: Sophie Adenot, en mission dans la Station spatiale internationale (ISS), est devenue mardi la première astronaute française à sortir dans l'espace, en compagnie de l'Américain Anil Menon.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Patrick Vieira est nommé sélectionneur du Sénégal en remplacement de Pape Thiaw
Sélectionneur du Sénégal, le nouveau défi de Patrick Vieira avec les Lions de la Téranga
france24fr.description: Patrick Vieira a été nommé, mardi, sélectionneur des Lions de la Téranga par la Fédération sénégalaise de football. Le successeur de Pape Thiaw sur le banc du Sénégal aura notamment la lourde tâche d'insuffler une nouvelle dynamique après le cuisant revers face à la Belgique lors du Mondial 2026.

france24fr.title: En direct : Sophie Adenot sort dans l'espace, une première pour une Française
Sophie Adenot dans l’espace : quel est le programme de sa sortie spatiale ?
france24fr.description: Sophie Adenot, en mission dans la Station spatiale internationale (ISS), doit devenir mardi la première astronaute française à sortir dans l'espace, en compagnie de l'Américain Anil Menon. Les précisions d'Hervé Stevenin, instructeur au centre d'entraînement des astronautes européens.

france24fr.title: CAN féminine 2026 : retour triomphal des championnes d'Afrique au Cameroun
france24fr.description: Le Cameroun célèbre ses nouvelles championnes d’Afrique. Les Lionnes Indomptables, sacrées pour la première fois après leur victoire 3-0 face au Malawi, ont été accueillies par des milliers de supporters à Yaoundé. Retour en images sur cette journée de fête.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Moyen-Orient en direct : les États-Unis accusent Israël de frappes en Syrie
Mort de Tupac Shakur : le procès s’ouvre sur la thèse d’une vengeance de gang
france24fr.description:
Près de 30 ans après la mort de Tupac Shakur, le procès de Duane Davis s’est ouvert à Las Vegas. 
 
L’accusation affirme que le meurtre du rappeur relevait d’une vengeance de gang, tandis que la défense dénonce un dossier sans preuves matérielles suffisantes.

france24fr.title: Tupac Shakur a été tué à cause d'une "vengeance" de gang, selon l'accusation
france24fr.description: L'ancien membre de gang accusé d'avoir orchestré le meurtre de Tupac Shakur a agi par "vengeance", car il nourrissait une "colère viscérale" à l'encontre du rappeur pour avoir humilié son neveu, et a tout avoué lui-même, a soutenu lundi l'accusation.

france24fr.title: Zambie : le président sortant Hichilema réélu dans un contexte confus
france24fr.description: Le président sortant de Zambie, Hakainde Hichilema, a été réélu mardi pour un deuxième mandat, dans une confusion politique inhabituelle pour ce pays d'Afrique australe riche en cuivre, avec notamment des arrestations d'opposants.

france24fr.title: À Séoul, la voyance passe à l'ère de l'intelligence artificielle
france24fr.description: À Séoul, les voyants traditionnels côtoient désormais une nouvelle génération de "devins" : des machines dopées à l’intelligence artificielle. Analyse du visage, avatars virtuels…La technologie s’empare des traditions pour proposer une nouvelle façon de lire l’avenir.

france24fr.title: La Syrie condamne à mort Wassim al-Assad, cousin du président déchu
france24fr.description: Wassim al-Assad, cousin du président syrien déchu Bachar al-Assad, a été condamné à mort mardi par la justice syrienne. Il a été reconnu coupable d'actes qualifiés de crimes contre l'humanité et de crimes de guerre.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : comment le pays a-t-il perdu le contrôle de l’épidémie ?
france24fr.description: En trois mois, l’épidémie d’Ebola en République démocratique du Congo a fait 2 325 morts et près de 5 000 cas confirmés, devenant la plus meurtrière jamais enregistrée dans le pays. Le virus tue désormais près d’une personne toutes les 30 minutes. Comment en est-on arrivé là ? Les explications de Sylvie Briand, scientifique en chef de l'OMS.

france24fr.title: En Russie, le vice-président du parti anti-guerre condamné
france24fr.description: Le vice-président du parti antiguerre russe Iabloko, Lev Chlosberg, a été condamné lundi à 11 ans et un mois de prison pour des propos critiquant l'offensive de Moscou en Ukraine, lancée en février 2022.

france24fr.title: Pologne : des fouilles archéologiques font ressurgir le ghetto de Varsovie
france24fr.description: À Varsovie, des archéologues mettent au jour les vestiges d’édifices détruits par les nazis en 1943. Ces fouilles permettent de documenter l’histoire de la communauté juive de la capitale et de préserver les traces du ghetto. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: L'Ukraine a lancé 620 drones sur la région de Moscou, selon les autorités russes
france24fr.description: L'Ukraine ​a lancé 620 drones sur Moscou et ses environs dans la nuit ​de lundi à mardi, a déclaré le maire de la capitale russe, dans le cadre de l'une des plus importantes attaques aériennes menées par Kyiv, ​tandis ‌que la Crimée, annexée par la Russie, a ⁠subi des coupures d'électricité à la suite des frappes.

france24fr.title: Sophie Adenot va devenir la première Française à sortir dans l'espace
france24fr.description: Sophie Adenot, en mission dans la Station spatiale internationale (ISS), doit devenir mardi la première astronaute française à sortir dans l'espace, en compagnie de l'Américain Anil Menon.

nzz.title: Wieder ein Legionellen-Ausbruch: In Wetzikon häufen sich die Fälle, die Ursache ist aber noch nicht klar
nzz.description: Die Gesundheitsdirektion untersucht, warum es in Wetzikon zu auffällig vielen Ansteckungen mit Legionellen kommt. Die Bakterien können schwere Lungenentzündungen verursachen.

nzz.title: Der «Spiegel» setzt AfD-Mann Ulrich Siegmund als «gefährlichsten Mann Deutschlands» auf die Frontseite. Die AfD freut’s
nzz.description: Donald Trump als IS-Mörder, Giorgia Meloni und Gendersprech-Gegner als «heimliche Hitler»: Je mehr die Auflage des «Spiegels» sinkt, desto schriller werden seine Titelgeschichten. Die jüngste sorgt für landesweite Aufregung.

nzz.title: Wer sich nicht benimmt, fliegt raus: Schweden hat seine Migrationspolitik deutlich verschärft
nzz.description: Lange hielt sich Schweden für eine humanitäre Supermacht. Doch die Politik der offenen Türen brachte Probleme mit sich. Davon könnten die rechtspopulistischen Schwedendemokraten bei der Parlamentswahl im September profitieren.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Kultur: Kanye West plant Konzerte in Russland. Und träumt davon, Wladimir Putin zu treffen
DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Krise in Syrien: Asad-Cousin zum Tode verurteilt +++ Israel greift Militärflugplatz in Syrien an
nzz.description: Seit dem Sturz des langjährigen Machthabers Bashar al-Asad Ende 2024 erlebt Syrien ungewisse Zeiten. So zeigt sich zurzeit die Lage.

nzz.title: Warum Israel plötzlich um und mit Amerika kämpfen muss
nzz.description: Tel Avivs Vizebürgermeister will sich mit dem New Yorker Verwaltungschef prügeln, Netanyahu druckt Wahlplakate mit Zohran Mamdani neben Khamenei und Erdogan. Was wie Klamauk wirkt, ist Ausdruck eines tieferen Bruchs.

nzz.title: Ein Moskauer Top-Ökonom spricht von einer Niederlage Russlands gegen die Ukraine – und wird entlassen
nzz.description: Andrei Klepatsch ist seit den 1990er Jahren ein Technokrat in der russischen Wirtschaftselite. In einer Rede zeigt er nüchtern auf, was Bilanzen über Russlands Wirtschaft erzählen. Moskaus Abnutzungskrieg sei nicht zu gewinnen, sagt er. Sein Rausschmiss folgt prompt. Für Kritik jeglicher Art ist in Russland längst kein Platz mehr.

nzz.title: Heimat, Heiligtum, Hoffnung – warum ein Baum unsterblich wird
nzz.description: Ein Baobab in Madagaskar stirbt, ein berühmter Baum in England wird gefällt. Und die Menschen trauern. Was macht einzelne Bäume so besonders?

nzz.title: Der lange Flug des Rainer-Marc Frey: Warum der Financier und Hobbypilot jetzt Hauptaktionär von Leonteq ist
nzz.description: Der Milliardär löst die Raiffeisen als wichtigster Aktionär beim Zürcher Finanzunternehmen ab. Für den passionierten Piloten soll sich seine bereits 2017 eingegangene Beteiligung endlich auszahlen.

nzz.title: Charmeoffensive für Davos: Guy Parmelin weibelt bei Larry Fink, damit das WEF in der Schweiz bleibt
nzz.description: Der Stiftungsrat des WEF entscheidet heute Nachmittag, wie es mit der Organisation weitergehen soll. In Bern kam es derweil zu einem Treffen zwischen Guy Parmelin und den beiden Co-Präsidenten Larry Fink und André Hoffmann.

nzz.title: Zürich verzeichnet mehr leerstehende Wohnungen. Die Zahlen sind mit Vorbehalt zu geniessen
nzz.description: 4200 Wohnungen waren im Kanton Zürich Anfang Juni unbewohnt. In den Städten Zürich und Winterthur ist die Quote weiterhin tief.

nzz.title: Das Internet-Ereignis des Sommers: Ein Amerikaner läuft vier Tage lang schlaflos im Kreis – und gewinnt deutsches Extremrennen
nzz.description: Mark Dowdle setzt sich am Last Soul Ultra gegen den Deutschen Ayyoub El Osrouti durch. Die beiden rannten über 600 Kilometer weit. Tausende schauten zu.

nzz.title: Inszenierte Anschläge gegen Journalisten in Italien: der Fall Ranucci als politische Spielerei
nzz.description: Italien wundert sich in diesem Sommer über zwei Fake-Anschläge. Einer davon galt dem bekannten Investigativjournalisten Sigfrido Ranucci. Es ist, als hätte das Land seine blutige Geschichte vergessen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Fähre kann keine schweren Lastwagen mehr transportieren
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Gasspeicher liegen deutlich unter Normalniveau – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

observador.title: Kanye West anuncia dois concertos na Rússia
observador.description: O artista agora conhecido como Ye anunciou duas datas em São Petersburgo. Desde o início da invasão da Ucrânia que os artistas ocidentais de maior relevo não atuam no país.

observador.title: Macau quer Portugal a ajudar expansão da medicina chinesa
observador.description: Plano será apoiar os produtos na sua expansão internacional, tendo como ponto de entrada os países da CPLP. Atualmente, já têm medicamentos registados em Moçambique e no Brasil.

observador.title: Portugal 2030 ultrapassa 20% de execução até julho
observador.description: O programa Portugal 2030 já ultrapassou os 4,7 mil milhões de euros de fundo executado. Já as aprovações ultrapassaram os 13.600 milhões de euros, o equivalente a 59,2% da dotação programada.

observador.title: Vila Pouca de Aguiar abre concurso de 1,3 milhões para saúde
observador.description: Depois de os dois últimos concursos terem ficado desertos, a autarca aumentou a verba em 400 mil euros, para "responder ao mercado". Espera que concurso avance, visto que o PRR está em fase final.

observador.title: Sismo na Indonésia causa 70 mortos e 22 mil deslocados
observador.description: O balanço anterior dava conta de 68 mortos, mas o número de deslocados em Flores mais do que duplicou em relação a segunda-feira. As estimativas variam em relação ao número de feridos.

observador.title: 14h. Incêndio em Torre de Moncorvo com três frentes ativas
observador.description: No terreno estão mais de 400 operacionais, apoiados por 135 veículos e 5 meios aéreos. Ainda, arranca hoje o julgamento que opõe 29 estados norte-americanos à Meta.

observador.title: Movimento faz queixa a Bruxelas devido a projeto urbanístico
observador.description: O Artilharia Um alega violação da Diretiva Europeia relativa à "avaliação dos efeitos de determinados projetos públicos e privados no ambiente". Em causa está um projeto promovido pelo Novo Banco.

observador.title: Preços na produção industrial aumentam 5,8% em julho
observador.description: A evolução do Índice de Preços na Produção Industrial foi determinada principalmente pelos agrupamentos "energia" e "bens intermédios", com 2,6 e 2,3 pontos percentuais para a variação total.

observador.title: Terceiro suspeito de roubar barras de ouro em preventiva
observador.description: O roubo das barras de ouro, avaliadas em cerca de 342 mil euros, aconteceu no dia 6 de agosto. A vítima transportava o ouro numa mochila e preparava-se para as vender na rua onde aconteceu o crime.

observador.title: Preventiva para suspeito de roubar dois jovens no Porto
observador.description: O suspeito de 45 anos terá ameaçado os jovens e coagido-os a entregar-lhe o dinheiro que tinham com eles. O homem foi detido e a quantia roubada foi apreendida pela PSP.

observador.title: A goleada do Benfica afasta mesmo os "fantasmas"?
observador.description: As águias marcaram 7 golos ao Casa Pia numa demonstração de força em Rio Maior. Que sinais deixa esta goleada? Ainda os novos episódios da "revolução de Alvalade" e o futuro de Rodrigo Mora.

observador.title: Morreram Mathilde Favier e Nicolas Altmayer
observador.description: O carro em que seguiam a RP da Dior, responsável por conectar a maison com as principais estrelas da atualidade, e o marido, foi atingido por um camião esta segunda-feira.

observador.title: Évora. Detido por maus-tratos à ex-companheira perante filho
observador.description: Está fortemente indiciado que o suspeito manteve maus-tratos psicológicos e físicos à ex-mulher, praticados na presença do filho. Os factos ocorreram inicialmente num país estrangeiro.

observador.title: 13h. REN. IL quer ouvir ministro das Finanças no Parlamento
observador.description: A Iniciativa Liberal defende que pode estar em causa o "sacrifício de dinheiro dos contribuintes de forma irrefletida". Ainda, estão mobilizados mais de 400 operacionais no fogo em Torre de Moncorvo.

observador.title: Bruxelas promete plano para reforçar resiliência climática
observador.description: A porta-voz da Comissão Europeia salientou que a Europa está a "aquecer duas vezes mais rápido" do que os outros continentes. Vários membros da UE registaram este verão novos recordes de temperatura.

observador.title: IL quer ouvir ministro sobre reentrada do Estado na REN
observador.description: Liberais dizem que efeito mais problemático da reentrada é a "decisão resultante da estratégia do Governo para reduzir o preço da energia" e alertam para descida de ações da empresa depois do anúncio.

observador.title: Rei Harald V da Noruega tem doença sanguínea autoimune
observador.description: O monarca mais velho da Europa foi internado em Oslo para tratar retenção de líquidos causada por corticóides. A doença de base, uma anemia hemolítica, era até agora desconhecida do público.

observador.title: Israel sugere novo plano para desarmar o Hamas
observador.description: Entre as alterações está a obrigação da retirada de Israel acontecer apenas depois de o Hamas entregar todas as armas em Gaza. Ainda, Irão tenta reforçar laços com Iraque.

spiegel.title: China: Animationsfilm »Niu Lai« wird zum Megaerfolg – weil er so schlecht ist
spiegel.description: Hässliche Animationen und schwer nachzuvollziehende Handlung: Der Film »Niu Lai« floppte zunächst. Dank vieler nicht ganz ernst gemeinter Bewertungen im Netz ist in China aber nun ein Hype um das Werk entstanden.

spiegel.title: Thüringen: Voigt betont Zusammenhalt seiner Brombeerkoalition
spiegel.description: Der Streit im BSW erschüttert die Regierung in Thüringen. CDU-Ministerpräsident Mario Voigt gibt sich demonstrativ gelassen und sagt, er wolle seine Koalition »nicht zum Spielball parteitaktischer Manöver machen«.

spiegel.title: Fußball: Niclas Füllkrug kehrt zurück zu Werder Bremen
spiegel.description: Ein Transfer, der an der Weser gute Erinnerungen weckt: Niclas Füllkrug wechselt erneut zu Werder Bremen, wo er einst zum Nationalspieler reifte. Für den Deal habe er »wirtschaftliche Abstriche« gemacht, sagt der Stürmer.

spiegel.title: Nordrhein-Westfalen: Großbrand in Belgien stinkt bis Köln
spiegel.description: Die Kölner Feuerwehr spricht von einer »großräumigen Geruchslage«, doch die Flammen im belgischen Naturschutzgebiet sind offenbar weitgehend unter Kontrolle. Nun sollen Schneisen Deutschland vor dem Brand schützen.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Koblenz: Angeklagter gesteht Mord an US-Studentin Amy Lopez
spiegel.description: 1994 wurde die junge US-Amerikanerin Amy Lopez in Koblenz Opfer eines Gewaltverbrechens. Nun steht der mutmaßliche Täter vor Gericht. Auch sein Verteidiger erwartet eine Verurteilung wegen Mordes.

spiegel.title: Pflegegrad schnell beantragen, empfiehlt der Sozialverband
spiegel.description: In der Merz-Koalition gibt es den Plan, dass künftig weniger Menschen als pflegebedürftig gelten sollen. Der Sozialverband VdK rät Betroffenen, vorher noch zu handeln.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Fehlende Patriot-Raketen sind Kyjiws größte Schwachstelle
spiegel.description: Russland greift mit immer mehr ballistischen Raketen an, die Ukraine ist überfordert: Die einzig wirksame Abwehrwaffe steht kaum mehr zur Verfügung. Donald Trump versprach Abhilfe, rudert nun aber zurück.

spiegel.title: Erstes Verliebtsein: Gibt es die erste Liebe zwischen Teenagern noch?
spiegel.description: Männer und Frauen können nicht mehr gut miteinander. Oder? Hier erzählen die Teenager Sina und Nico, was ihre Beziehung belastet und wer ihre Vorbilder in Sachen Liebe sind.

spiegel.title: USA: Wie Superreiche in Kalifornien gegen die Milliardärssteuer kämpfen
spiegel.description: Die Debatte über eine Vermögensteuer für Superreiche in Kalifornien sorgt im Silicon Valley für Unruhe. Mit viel Geld versuchen Milliardäre, die Abstimmung im November für sich zu entscheiden.

spiegel.title: Syrien: Wassim al-Assad zum Tode verurteilt
spiegel.description: Auch gegen Wassim al-Assad, einen Cousin des früheren syrischen Diktators, ist nun die Todesstrafe verhängt worden. Anders als der nach Russland geflüchtete Ex-Machthaber war der Angeklagte im Prozess anwesend.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Justizminister Darmanin verzichtet auf Kandidatur bei Präsidentschaftswahl
spiegel.description: In Frankreich wird im kommenden Jahr ein neues Staatsoberhaupt gewählt. Justizminister Darmanin sorgt sich vor einem möglichen Duell der Extreme in der Stichwahl – und stellt deswegen eigene Ambitionen zurück.

spiegel.title: Gianni Infantino: Niersbach sieht Concacaf-Chef Victor Montagliani als Alternative
spiegel.description: Noch gibt es keinen Gegenkandidaten, um Gianni Infantino als Fifa-Chef abzuwählen. Für den früheren DFB-Funktionär Wolfgang Niersbach wäre Concacaf-Chef Victor Montagliani ein geeigneter Nachfolger.

spiegel.title: Sifnos: Brautpaar stirbt nach Hubschrauberabsturz auf griechischer Insel
spiegel.description: In Griechenland ist ein Hubschrauber beim Landeanflug abgestürzt und explodiert, alle drei Insassen sind tot. Das britische Paar an Bord wollte offenbar seine Flitterwochen in der Ägäis verbringen.

spiegel.title: Drohnenabwehr in Deutschland: Forschungszentrum in Sachsen-Anhalt nimmt Arbeit auf
spiegel.description: Innenminister Dobrindt hat ein Forschungszentrum eröffnet, das Möglichkeiten für die Drohnenabwehr entwickeln soll. Erst vor zwei Wochen entging der Flughafen Leipzig bei einem Vorfall knapp einer Katastrophe.

spiegel.title: Lena Headey: Schauspielerin aus »Game of Thrones« fand Sexszenen »wirklich erschreckend«
spiegel.description: Es sei eine Art Initiationsritus gewesen: Als junge Schauspielerin setzten intime Szenen Lena Headey unter Druck. Sie erinnert sich an Alkohol und Tränen zu Hause.

spiegel.title: Alexandra Popp: Der glückliche Abstieg in die Regionalliga
spiegel.description: Dritte Liga statt Champions League: Alexandra Popp ist abgestiegen, um für ihren Lieblingsclub BVB zu kicken. Ein Schritt in die sportliche Bedeutungslosigkeit. Und sie wirkt: glücklich.

spiegel.title: Spirit Airlines: Google kauft interne Daten von insolventer US-Airline, um seine KI zu trainieren
spiegel.description: Mails, Teams-Chats und Präsentationen: Für diese und weitere Unternehmensdaten der gescheiterten Fluggesellschaft Spirit Airlines hat Google Millionen gezahlt. Der Techkonzern will damit seine KI verbessern.

letemps.title: Genève accueillera dès 2027 le siège mondial d’un organisme pour des investissements durables face au climat
letemps.description:
L’ISSB, qui établit des standards internationaux pour mesurer l’empreinte environnementale des entreprises, installera son cinquième bureau important à Genève. Cette structure soutenue par le G7 et le G20 est financée jusqu’en 2031

La Genève internationale va accueillir dès l’année prochaine le siège d’une entité qui établit un cadre pour des investissements financiers adaptés face au changem

letemps.title: En Suisse, les principaux risques de blanchiment d’argent proviennent des sociétés étrangères
letemps.description:
Firmes étrangères et trusts sont pointés du doigt par un rapport de la Confédération. En matière de financement du terrorisme, une lacune dans la surveillance des fondations et des associations est constatée

Cent neuf pages publiées uniquement en allemand. Il en faut moins pour décourager la majorité des francophones de ce pays de lire le dernier rapport sur les risques de blanchiment d’argen

letemps.description:
OPINION. La politique si glorifiée des «bons offices» implique de dialoguer avec toutes les parties, or la Suisse ne fait que ménager la politique d’annexion du gouvernement Netanyahou, écrit l'ancien directeur de la DDC en Palestine Mario Carera

phys-org.title: The link between incoherent beliefs and conspiracism
phys-org.description: Simultaneous belief in logically incompatible claims is linked to conspiratorial thinking, according to a study that models belief using a Bayesian framework.

phys-org.title: Tomato roots reveal hidden steps in 400-million-year-old fungal partnership
phys-org.description: Scientists at VIB and Ghent University have produced the first high-resolution, cell-by-cell map of how tomato roots respond to colonization by arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi. These ancient fungal partners help plants absorb nutrients from the soil.

phys-org.title: Unusual superconductivity could emerge in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral graphene
phys-org.description: Superconductors are materials in which electrical current flows with a resistance of zero, typically below specific temperatures. In conventional superconductors, this state of matter emerges when two electrons bind together at low temperatures, forming so-called Cooper pairs.

phys-org.title: Webb captures clearest image yet of the Lion Nebula
phys-org.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope recently imaged NGC 2392 (also known as the Lion Nebula), named for its distinctive appearance, which resembles a lion's face seen head-on.

phys-org.title: AI reconstructs hidden history of Earth's mantle flow from surface clues
phys-org.description: The mantle, a rocky layer accounting for more than 80% of Earth's volume, circulates at rates of only a few centimeters per year. This circulation drives plate tectonics and influences major geological phenomena such as earthquakes and volcanic activity. Despite its fundamental importance, the history of mantle circulation remains poorly understood because direct observations of the deep Earth are extremely limited. Currently, scientists rely on geological records of past surface movements

phys-org.title: Drier soils may turn late summer into prolonged extreme heat
phys-org.description: The summers of recent years have been hot, but not unusual from a meteorological perspective. According to researchers at Leipzig University, though, the next extreme summer would far exceed anything we have experienced so far.

phys-org.title: New gene activity tool measures biological age of cells and screens aging-related compounds
phys-org.description: Researchers at Karolinska Institutet and Stockholm University have developed a new tool that estimates a cell's biological age by analyzing its gene activity. In an article published in the journal Advanced Science, they also demonstrate how the tool can be used to identify substances that influence cellular aging.

phys-org.title: Aerial imagery maps hurricane wind damage and shows stronger building codes work
phys-org.description: Massive storms like Hurricane Katrina in 2005, which caused more than $100 billion in damage, were once considered lifetime events. Increasingly, however, they are becoming the norm: a direct result of climate change, which has made large storms more frequent, intense and slower-moving, deepening their impact.

phys-org.title: Distinct neurons drive mice's social sounds and squeaks
phys-org.description: Mice use almost completely distinct sets of neurons for their two different types of vocalizations—the squeaks they produce when in distress or fighting and the whistle-like ultrasonic vocalizations they use when communicating socially, Cornell neuroscientists have found. The discovery is a step toward understanding how the brain is organized to control vocalization in mammals, including humans.

phys-org.title: Ruby-forming mineral found by Mars rover hints at violent impacts
phys-org.description: So far, most of the minerals found on Mars tell a story of lava poured out by ancient volcanoes, followed by long stretches in which water trickled through and slowly reshaped the rock. However, some rocks scattered across the Martian surface seem to hint at a different geological history—carrying the same material that forms rubies and sapphires.

phys-org.title: Caregivers are active agents in their infants' learning, but interactions differ across cultures
phys-org.description: A baby sits on the floor and reaches toward a red ball on the floor and grunts. The mother responds, "Do you see the ball?" She picks it up, holds it in front of the baby and says, "Do you want to hold the ball?" The baby shrieks in excitement as the mother hands the ball to the baby.

phys-org.title: Nuking an asteroid on short notice could save us
phys-org.description: Readers of a certain age will remember a golden era of asteroid films, capped by two with very different endings. "Deep Impact" drove home the devastating consequences of letting a large piece of rock hit our planet, whereas "Armageddon," though arguably the kitschier of the two films, was an uplifting story about technical ingenuity and sacrifice.

phys-org.title: A new approach to building noise-resistant quantum sensors
phys-org.description: Quantum sensors, devices that collect measurements by exploiting quantum-mechanical phenomena, could potentially detect extremely weak magnetic, gravitational and electromagnetic signals with greater sensitivity than classical sensors. Some quantum sensors leverage entanglement, a phenomenon that prompts distant particles to become so strongly linked that the physical state of one particle dictates the state of the others.

phys-org.title: Soot spikes from traffic and holiday bonfires emerge in Addis Ababa air record
phys-org.description: An air pollution monitoring network has provided one of the most detailed long-term views yet of the role of black carbon, or soot produced by fires, diesel vehicles and other combustion sources, in Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa. The detailed measurements show how pollution changes by time of day and season, including increases associated with rush-hour traffic and holiday celebrations. The findings are relevant to cities around the world, including in the United States.

phys-org.title: School's back, stress doesn't have to be
phys-org.description: Going back to school can be an exciting time for students from elementary school through college, whether it's finding the perfect outfit to wear on the first day, returning to campus or filling a chalkboard with career dreams.

phys-org.title: 'Ecological engineers' an existential threat to wildlife of iconic wetland
phys-org.description: A study examining how feral water buffalo interact with landscapes has uncovered the pest's disastrous impacts on northern long-necked turtles in the Top End's tropical wetlands.

phys-org.title: How body size and habitat shape the vocal repertoires of primates
phys-org.description: Biologists, zoologists and psychologists have been trying to trace the origins of human language for centuries. One well-known theory, known as the social brain hypothesis, suggests that increasingly complex social lives prompted primates to evolve increasingly larger brains, which in turn led to increasingly advanced communication skills.

phys-org.title: How tomato 'golden hour' research could help crops survive heat waves and drought
phys-org.description: What if the secret to drought-resistant crops isn't how much water plants use, but when they use it? A new study identifies a daily window that could help breeders develop tomatoes that better withstand drought without sacrificing yield.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: Iceland Belongs in the Eurozone
proj-syn.description: In evaluating the trade-offs of joining the European Union and giving up their own currency, Icelanders must recognize that the costs of eurozone membership are smaller than what past data suggest. If anything, being within the eurosystem would make a repeat of Iceland's post-2008 banking crisis exceedingly unlikely.

proj-syn.title: Zhu Rongji’s Legacy of Demographic Decline
proj-syn.description: Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji’s recent death elicited widespread accolades for his role in pushing the market-oriented reforms that unleashed decades of economic growth. But Zhu also oversaw two major policy shifts that have had dire implications for China’s demographic outlook.

proj-syn.title: The Global Land Agenda’s Moment of Truth
proj-syn.description: As delegates gather this week in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, for the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification, momentum is building toward a more ambitious global response to land degradation. In fact, there are five promising signs that this time could be different.

proj-syn.title: How Trump Is Reinvigorating Democracy
proj-syn.description: After a year of commentators lamenting the extent to which Donald Trump had emboldened the world’s autocrats, the political tables may have begun to turn. Not only is Trump deeply unpopular globally, but any government that gets into bed with him is effectively offering proof of its own corruption.

proj-syn.title: Ebola is Back-and the IMF’s Relief Fund Is Empty
proj-syn.description: Once again, the International Monetary Fund finds itself begging for resources to support poor countries facing a public-health emergency. It is an old problem, but one for which there is a remarkably simple solution.

proj-syn.title: What Should Be Done About Asia’s Undervalued Currencies?
proj-syn.description: Those who worry that the renminbi, yen, and won are undervalued vis-à-vis the dollar are usually focused on the large trade and current-account surpluses that China, Japan, and Korea run with the US. But coordinated intervention in currency markets will not address the fundamentals underlying these imbalances.

proj-syn.title: How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse
proj-syn.description: Even if AI-related job displacement is less severe than many feared, corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing its effects in the name of social solidarity. To that end, governments should consider what policy incentives are in place, and large employers should consider their own long-term interests.

proj-syn.title: The Making and Remaking of Chinese Totalitarianism
proj-syn.description: For decades, the West assumed that economic growth would turn China into a more open, liberal society, much as it did South Korea and Taiwan. Instead, China’s totalitarian institutions proved remarkably resilient, surviving decades of reform and reasserting themselves under President Xi Jinping.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Not Forget Multilateral Institutions
proj-syn.description: The roadmap for middle-power action that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb recently laid out calls for countries that share interests to create ad hoc coalitions. But to be effective, these coalitions must work as much as possible within existing multilateral institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.
